title: Pharma water system services, URS to service | Aquemi
meta: Design, fabrication, FAT/SAT, IQ/OQ/PQ, service and upgrades for PW, WFI and pure steam, on one traceability record from URS on, per EU GMP Annex 15.
headline: One team and one traceable record, from your URS to the last service visit
lead: We carry your Purified Water (PW), Water for Injection (WFI) or pure steam system from user requirement specification (URS) to service on one traceability matrix. Tell us where your project stands and we start there.

blocks.h: What leaves each stage, and who signs it
blocks.intro: EU GMP Annex 15, 3.2 makes your URS the reference for the whole lifecycle. Each requirement gets an ID at first review and keeps it in every document.

items.d: Compliance matrix, basis of design, P&IDs, functional specification, risk assessment. Your quality unit approves design qualification (DQ). Annex 15, 3.2 and 3.3; ICH Q9(R1).
Material log with EN 10204 3.1 certificates, weld maps and log, borescope, finish, passivation and pressure test records. You set hold points. ASME BPE.
Protocol approved before execution, executed protocol with raw data, deviation log, summary report. Both parties sign release to ship. Annex 15, 3.4 to 3.6.
Installation and commissioning records, SAT on your feed water and utilities, traceability matrix with leveraged tests flagged. You sign the SAT report. Annex 15, 3.7.
C&Q plan, IQ and OQ protocols and reports, draft operating procedures, training records. Your quality unit approves each. Annex 15, 3.9 to 3.12.

items.t: PQ: three phases, at least 12 months
items.d: PQ protocol and sampling plan, phase reports, alert and action levels. Your quality unit releases water by phase. WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3.
Signed report per visit, calibration certificates with as-found and as-left values, like-for-like parts record, annual system review. USP <645>, <643>; Annex 15, 4.1.
Assessment with gap list and options, each with downtime and requalification scope your quality unit approves. Annex 15, section 11; 21 CFR Part 11.

blocks.body: Each plan states in writing the on-site response for a critical fault, from [severity 1 on-site response time, hours], the visit scope and calibration intervals. Every visit runs under your change control.

blocks.h: Questions engineering, validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Can the company that builds the system also qualify it?
items.a: Yes, under your control. Annex 15, 2.6 asks that third-party protocols are confirmed by your own personnel before approval. Your quality unit approves every protocol before execution and every report after it; we write and execute. If your procedures require an independent contractor, we hand them the traceability matrix and records written to be leveraged.

items.q: Can we buy one stage only?
items.a: Yes. Each service has its own first step and its own documents. The joining table above shows what we need when we join part way.

items.q: Do you work on systems built by other suppliers?
items.a: Yes, for [makes and equipment types serviced]. We start with an assessment or condition survey: without the as-built state and a year of data, a quote either carries contingency or leaves validation gaps to be found during the work. For a fault or planned visit, use the service request form with make and model; no Aquemi serial number is needed.

items.q: How long from URS to water released for use?
items.a: For a packaged PW skid, allow [design to DQ, weeks] for design, [approved design to FAT, weeks] to FAT and [IQ/OQ on site, days] for IQ and OQ on site. PQ runs at least two phases of two weeks; phase 2 water can be used in production if your quality unit accepts the data (WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3, 11.3).

items.q: What does one traceability matrix look like in practice?
items.a: URS-012: PW conductivity ≤ 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C at every point of use (USP <645> stage 1). It becomes a functional specification divert clause, numbered sensor tees on weld maps, a FAT divert test flagged for OQ leverage, raw non-compensated readings at SAT and OQ, 12 months or more of PQ data and cell constant checks within ± 2 % per calibration.

items.q: Do we have to use your document templates?
items.a: No. We write IQ, OQ and PQ documents in your templates where you have them, and keep our requirement IDs inside them so the trace survives. Where you have none, we use ours, and your quality unit approves the templates once, at the start.

items.q: Who is our contact across the stages?
items.a: [project contact from URS review to handover] The traceability matrix and the turnover package go with the system, so the service engineer starts from the same record as the project team.
